new_candidates.body:
### Intro

Hi!

I am a fresh PhD graduate from Inria (France). I use MuJoCo for reinforcement learning research, through Gymnasium's MuJoCo tasks and MJX.

### My setup

MuJoCo and MuJoCo MJX 4.0.1 (the colliders involved are unchanged on main, 71bc51c), Python API, JAX 0.12, CPU, float64 (`jax_enable_x64`), macOS 15 on Apple Silicon. Also seen with 3.7 to 3.10 on Linux x86_64.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

At the same poses, MJX's three capsule colliders give contacts that differ from C MuJoCo's. I expected `dist`, `pos` and `frame` to match `mj_forward`'s to floating-point precision, as every other primitive pair I checked does (plane-sphere, sphere-sphere, plane-box, plane-cylinder, plane-ellipsoid: 1e-15).

1. **`sphere_capsule` and `capsule_capsule`, closest points (not reported before, as far as I can find).** `math.closest_segment_point` adds 1e-6 to `dot(ab, ab)`, and `math.closest_segment_to_segment_points` adds 1e-6 to its denominator and resolves clipping differently from `mjc_segWeights`. On capsules of half-length 0.1, this moves the contact normal by up to 3e-4 (sphere-capsule) and 3e-3 (capsule-capsule). On Gymnasium's Humanoid-v5, whose limbs touch each other, one step then moved velocities by 2e-4.
2. **`plane_capsule`, tangent frame (#2774; open PR #3678).** MJX replaces the capsule axis projected on the plane by a fixed axis once the projection is shorter than 0.5. C keeps the projection (`mju_makeFrame`). Under a pyramidal cone this changes contact forces: on Gymnasium's Ant-v5, one step moved joint velocities by up to 0.86 when a leg stood steeply on the floor. #3678 fixes this; I add the Ant measurement as one more case where it matters.

Over 300 random poses per pair (two free bodies, random orientations, centres within a few radii), the largest frame gaps were 2.0 (plane-capsule), 3e-4 (sphere-capsule) and 3e-3 (capsule-capsule); `dist` and `pos` gaps were up to 4e-9 and 4e-6.

Also, for information: below `mjc_segWeights`' parallel cutoff, C makes two capsule-capsule contacts; MJX's `capsule_capsule` has `ncon=1`.

**Proposed fix.** I have a fix with tests ready (branch `fix/mjx-capsule-contacts` on YannBerthelot/mujoco). The three colliders follow C's rules (`mju_makeFrame`'s tangent, `mjraw_SphereCapsule`'s projection, `mjc_segWeights`), and the shared helpers in `math.py` are left alone. They then match C to 1e-14 in float64. A new test in `collision_driver_test.py` compares them with `mj_collision` on random poses. Its plane-capsule part overlaps #3678; I can drop it if #3678 lands first, or rebase onto it. Near-parallel capsules keep one contact; matching C's two would mean `ncon=2` for every capsule pair. Would you like the PR, and one contact or two there?

Separately, also for information: `mjx.forward` writes free joints' quaternions back normalised into `qpos`, while `mj_forward` leaves `qpos` as set.

Related: #3670 / #3782 fix MJX's ellipsoid pairs against C; this issue covers the capsule pairs, which they don't touch.

### Steps for reproduction

1. `pip install mujoco==4.0.1 mujoco-mjx==4.0.1`
2. Run the code below, with the model below in `XML`. It compares each contact's frame in MJX against C.
3. The leg-arm pair (two capsules) differs by 1.5e-3, and the floor-leg pair (a capsule 70 degrees from the floor) by 1.0. The other pairs agree to 1e-16.

```
world-leg        dist -0.0740  largest frame gap MJX vs C: 1.0e+00
world-arm        dist -0.0083  largest frame gap MJX vs C: 1.1e-16
leg-ball         dist -0.0316  largest frame gap MJX vs C: 2.6e-16
leg-arm          dist -0.0977  largest frame gap MJX vs C: 1.5e-03
```

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML
<mujoco>
  <option cone="pyramidal"/>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 .1"/>
    <body name="leg" pos="0 0 .07" euler="0 20 0">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="capsule" size=".05 .1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="ball" pos=".03 .02 .25">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="sphere" size=".07"/>
    </body>
    <body name="arm" pos="-.07 .03 .08" euler="40 60 0">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="capsule" size=".05 .1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```

</details>

### Code required for reproduction

<details>
<summary>Python</summary>

```python
import jax

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

import mujoco
import numpy as np
from mujoco import mjx

XML = """..."""  # the model above

model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(XML)
data = mujoco.MjData(model)
mujoco.mj_forward(model, data)

mjx_data = jax.jit(mjx.forward)(mjx.put_model(model), mjx.put_data(model, data))
mjx_contact = mjx_data._impl.contact

for c in data.contact[: data.ncon]:
    pair = tuple(sorted(c.geom))
    match = [
        i
        for i in range(mjx_contact.dist.shape[0])
        if tuple(sorted(np.asarray(mjx_contact.geom[i]))) == pair
        and abs(float(mjx_contact.dist[i]) - c.dist) < 1e-3
        and np.allclose(np.asarray(mjx_contact.pos[i]), c.pos, atol=1e-3)
    ][0]
    names = "-".join(model.body(model.geom_bodyid[g]).name for g in pair)
    gap = np.abs(np.asarray(mjx_contact.frame[match]).ravel() - c.frame).max()
    print(f"{names:16} dist {c.dist:+.4f}  largest frame gap MJX vs C: {gap:.1e}")
```

</details>

### Confirmations

- [x] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [x] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
new_candidates.title: MJX: capsule contacts differ from C MuJoCo (sphere-capsule and capsule-capsule closest points; plane-capsule frame, see #3678)

new_candidates.body:
### Summary

1. `writeGeometry` has no `GeometryType::CONVEX_MESH` branch, so `writeURDFFile` throws "Unknown geometry type, cannot write to XML!" for any scene graph with a `ConvexMesh`. That covers every support robot that sets `tesseract:make_convex="true"` (abb_irb2400, iiwa7, ...).
2. `writeURDFFile` drops the result of `doc.SaveFile(...)`. When the file can't be written, it returns normally and leaves no file.

### Reproducer

```cpp
tesseract::common::GeneralResourceLocator locator;
auto sg = tesseract::urdf::parseURDFFile(
    locator.locateResource("package://tesseract/support/urdf/abb_irb2400.urdf")->getFilePath(), locator);
tesseract::urdf::writeURDFFile(std::move(sg), "/tmp/abb_pkg", "abb_irb2400");
```

```text
exception: Could not write out urdf link
  exception: Could not write collision to XML for link `base_link`!
    exception: Could not write geometry for collision ''!
      exception: Unknown geometry type, cannot write to XML!
```

Save errors: make `<package>/urdf/<name>.urdf` a directory, then call `writeURDFFile`. It returns normally.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: the `ConvexMesh` is written as a `<mesh>` with `tesseract:make_convex="true"` and reads back as a `ConvexMesh`. Actual: an exception.
- Expected: an exception when the file can't be saved. Actual: silent success.

### Root cause (@ 7e2d803c)

- `urdf/src/geometry.cpp:191` `writeGeometry` dispatches on `geometry->getType()` and handles `MESH` (:270) but not `CONVEX_MESH`, which falls through to the `else` at :317. `writeMesh` already handles a `ConvexMesh`: it sets `tesseract:make_convex="true"` (`urdf/src/mesh.cpp:159`). It is just never reached.
- `urdf/src/urdf_parser.cpp:318` calls `doc.SaveFile(full_filepath.c_str())` and drops the `XMLError`.

### Proposed fix

- Add a `CONVEX_MESH` branch to `writeGeometry` that calls `writeMesh` the same way the `MESH` branch does.
- Throw when `SaveFile` doesn't return `XML_SUCCESS`, with the path and `doc.ErrorStr()` in the message.

A PR with the fix and tests follows (`write_geometry` gains a convex mesh case; new `write_urdf_convex_mesh` round-trips a `ConvexMesh` link through write → parse; `write_urdf_make_convex_robot` writes abb_irb2400; `write_urdf_save_failure`). All four fail on master and pass with the patch, and the rest of `tesseract_urdf_unit` passes (59/59).

### Not covered here: `COMPOUND_MESH`

A mesh resource with more than one sub-mesh parses into a `CompoundMesh` (`urdf/src/geometry.cpp:122`), and `writeGeometry` has no branch for that either. The same "Unknown geometry type" error therefore still hits lbr_iiwa_14_r820 (multi-mesh `.dae` visuals), car_seat_demo, pick_and_place_plan, puzzle_piece_workcell and scene_graph_example after the patch above. A `<geometry>` holds one `<mesh>`, so this needs a design decision. Writing one `<visual>` / `<collision>` per sub-mesh from `writeLink` would keep collision exact: each convex piece stays separate, where merging the pieces into one file would turn them into a single hull on re-parse. Happy to send that as a follow-up once the approach is agreed.
new_candidates.title: writeURDFFile fails for every robot loaded with `tesseract:make_convex`, and ignores save errors
